target_customer: Licensed California cannabis brands that need distribution, and licensed dispensaries that buy wholesale
problem: Cannabis brands struggled to move product to dispensaries across a fragmented, heavily regulated supply chain, and retailers had no single place to buy from many brands.
business_model: Licensed wholesale distribution and marketplace: fees and margin on goods moved, plus fulfillment, payments and financing services
product_category: Cannabis wholesale distribution and logistics marketplace

founders.name: Vince Ning
founders.background_notes: Per the Nabis About page and the Oct 2018 seed release. Education not found.

founders.name: Jun S. Lee
founders.background_notes: Named co-founder on the Nabis About page. The YC page lists only Vince Ning. Education not found.

competitors.name: HERBL
competitors.what: California cannabis distributor and supply chain company
competitors.traction_then: launched August 2018 per a search summary of trade coverage

competitors.name: INDUS Distribution
competitors.what: Distribution arm of vertically integrated cannabis company INDUS Holding

competitors.name: Wayv
competitors.what: Cannabis logistics and e-commerce platform for brands and retailers, founded by former Eaze CEO
competitors.traction_then: launched September 2019, charged brands a 15 percent fee

technical_complexity.rationale: Mostly operations, licensing and logistics with ordering software on top; the founders were engineers who first drove deliveries themselves.

defensibility.rationale: Distribution licenses, fleet and warehouse scale and brand and retailer relationships were costly to replicate, but California had roughly two distribution licenses per retailer in 2019 so rivals were many.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent absorbed the model through at least 2025; Nabis grew by adding warehouses and buying distribution assets such as Humble Cannabis Solutions and a New Jersey license, per search summaries of press releases with no dates confirmed.

market_need_then: California's adult-use market opened in January 2018 and brands had trouble getting product to dispensaries; the founders' idea began in 2017 when a friend with a pre-roll brand struggled to transport product, per CannabisNow.

branding.name_origin: Reported by Forbes network articles as an abbreviation of cannabis; not confirmed in an English original.

identity.logo: No source describing the logo found
identity.voice_and_tone: Positions itself as the FedEx or DHL of cannabis per founder interviews

branding.brand_signature: The 'FedEx of cannabis' positioning, called the Amazon Prime of cannabis by Forbes network coverage

brand_strength.rationale: Widely cited as the largest California cannabis wholesaler and covered by trade and business press, but no evidence of mascot, merch or community; the brand is B2B.

outcome_analysis: Nabis started with founders delivering cannabis themselves in California's newly legal market, raised a seed in late 2018 and a second round in March 2019, then a $23 million Series B in July 2021 and expanded to New York and Nevada. It is active with a reported team of about 700. No layoffs or shutdown were found in a search. Licensed scale, brand exclusives and logistics execution explain the growth.
notes: One outlet reports total raised of 33.4 million, which exceeds the rounds recorded (about 28.25 million); a roughly 5 million round, described by a search snippet as a Series A, is not found with a source and is not recorded. The 2019 release calls the 4 million round the second round, so stage is other. Competitor source dates are September 2019, a few months after the batch. Founding year conflicts (2017 idea, 2018 YC listing). Search results about 2023 to 2025 acquisitions were snippets without dates.
